review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

20:1.sourceText: Ὁμοία γάρ ἐστιν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν ἀνθρώπῳ οἰκοδεσπότῃ, ὅστις ἐξῆλθεν ἅμα πρωῒ μισθώσασθαι ἐργάτας εἰς τὸν ἀμπελῶνα αὐτοῦ.
20:1.targetText: “For the kingdom of heaven is like a landowner who went out early in the morning to hire workers for his vineyard.

groups.note: ἀνθρώπῳ οἰκοδεσπότῃ, literally "a man, a master of a house", is one idiom for a landowner.
ἅμα πρωῒ is one idiom for early in the morning; ἅμα alone does not mean early.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

20:2.sourceText: συμφωνήσας δὲ μετὰ τῶν ἐργατῶν ἐκ δηναρίου τὴν ἡμέραν ἀπέστειλεν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὸν ἀμπελῶνα αὐτοῦ.
20:2.targetText: He agreed to pay them a denarius for the day and sent them into his vineyard.

groups.note: μετὰ τῶν ἐργατῶν, "with the workers", becomes the object them of to pay.
ἐκ δηναρίου, "for a denarius", states the agreed price.
The accusative τὴν ἡμέραν, "the day", is rendered for the day.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the paying implied by the price phrase ἐκ δηναρίου.
English coordinator; the participle συμφωνήσας is rendered as the finite verb agreed.

20:3.sourceText: καὶ ἐξελθὼν περὶ τρίτην ὥραν εἶδεν ἄλλους ἑστῶτας ἐν τῇ ἀγορᾷ ἀργούς,
20:3.targetText: About the third hour he went out and saw others standing in the marketplace doing nothing.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί is not separately expressed in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English coordinator; the participle ἐξελθών is rendered as the finite verb went out.

20:4.sourceText: καὶ ἐκείνοις εἶπεν Ὑπάγετε καὶ ὑμεῖς εἰς τὸν ἀμπελῶνα, καὶ ὃ ἐὰν ᾖ δίκαιον δώσω ὑμῖν.
20:4.targetText: ‘You also go into my vineyard,’ he said, ‘and I will pay you whatever is right.’

groups.note: The article is rendered as the possessive my.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί is not separately expressed in this English wording.
BSB leaves the addressees ἐκείνοις ("to those") unexpressed.

20:5.sourceText: οἱ δὲ ἀπῆλθον. πάλιν δὲ ἐξελθὼν περὶ ἕκτην καὶ ἐνάτην ὥραν ἐποίησεν ὡσαύτως.
20:5.targetText: So they went.  He went out again about the sixth hour and the ninth hour and did the same thing.

groups.note: In οἱ δέ the article serves as the pronoun they.
One ὥραν serves both ordinals; English repeats hour.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English coordinator; the participle ἐξελθών is rendered as the finite verb went out.

20:6.sourceText: περὶ δὲ τὴν ἑνδεκάτην ἐξελθὼν εὗρεν ἄλλους ἑστῶτας, καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς Τί ὧδε ἑστήκατε ὅλην τὴν ἡμέραν ἀργοί;
20:6.targetText: About the eleventh hour he went out and found still others standing around. ‘Why have you been standing here all day long doing nothing?’ he asked.

groups.note: The feminine ordinal ἑνδεκάτην stands without ὥραν ("hour"), which English supplies.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The καί before λέγει is not expressed; BSB places he asked after the question.
BSB leaves the addressees αὐτοῖς ("to them") unexpressed.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds still to mark yet another group; the Greek has only ἄλλους ("others").
English coordinator; the participle ἐξελθών is rendered as the finite verb went out.

20:7.sourceText: λέγουσιν αὐτῷ Ὅτι οὐδεὶς ἡμᾶς ἐμισθώσατο. λέγει αὐτοῖς Ὑπάγετε καὶ ὑμεῖς εἰς τὸν ἀμπελῶνα.
20:7.targetText: ‘Because no one has hired us,’ they answered.  So he told them, ‘You also go into my vineyard.’

groups.note: The article is rendered as the possessive my.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the addressee αὐτῷ ("to him") unexpressed.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds a connective; the Greek clause has none.

20:8.sourceText: ὀψίας δὲ γενομένης λέγει ὁ κύριος τοῦ ἀμπελῶνος τῷ ἐπιτρόπῳ αὐτοῦ Κάλεσον τοὺς ἐργάτας καὶ ἀπόδος τὸν μισθόν, ἀρξάμενος ἀπὸ τῶν ἐσχάτων ἕως τῶν πρώτων.
20:8.targetText: When evening came, the owner of the vineyard said to his foreman, ‘Call the workers and pay them their wages, starting with the last ones hired and moving on to the first.’

groups.note: The genitive absolute ὀψίας γενομένης, "evening having come", supplies When.
The article is rendered as the possessive their.
ἕως, "as far as", is rendered and moving on to.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB follows the reading ἀπόδος αὐτοῖς ("pay them"); N1904 has no αὐτοῖς.
English adds hired to identify the last workers.

20:9.sourceText: ἐλθόντες δὲ οἱ περὶ τὴν ἑνδεκάτην ὥραν ἔλαβον ἀνὰ δηνάριον.
20:9.targetText: The workers who were hired about the eleventh hour came and each received a denarius.

groups.note: The article οἱ turns "about the eleventh hour" into a noun phrase: those (workers).

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a relative clause for the group the article phrase names.
English coordinator; the participle ἐλθόντες is rendered as the finite verb came.

20:10.sourceText: καὶ ἐλθόντες οἱ πρῶτοι ἐνόμισαν ὅτι πλεῖον λήμψονται· καὶ ἔλαβον τὸ ἀνὰ δηνάριον καὶ αὐτοί.
20:10.targetText: So when the original workers came, they assumed they would receive more. But each of them also received a denarius.

groups.note: The participle ἐλθόντες is rendered as a temporal clause.
The nominative αὐτοί, "they", is rendered of them after each (ἀνά).

unmappedSource.reason: The conjunction ὅτι ("that") is left implicit in English.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

20:11.sourceText: λαβόντες δὲ ἐγόγγυζον κατὰ τοῦ οἰκοδεσπότου
20:11.targetText: On receiving their pay, they began to grumble against the landowner.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the object of receiving, which the Greek leaves implicit.

20:12.sourceText: λέγοντες Οὗτοι οἱ ἔσχατοι μίαν ὥραν ἐποίησαν, καὶ ἴσους αὐτοὺς ἡμῖν ἐποίησας τοῖς βαστάσασι τὸ βάρος τῆς ἡμέρας καὶ τὸν καύσωνα.
20:12.targetText: ‘These men who were hired last worked only one hour,’ they said, ‘and you have made them equal to us who have borne the burden and the scorching heat of the day.’

groups.note: The article with the participle, "the ones who bore", is rendered who have borne.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a relative clause to identify the last workers.
English adds only for emphasis.

20:13.sourceText: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς ἑνὶ αὐτῶν εἶπεν Ἑταῖρε, οὐκ ἀδικῶ σε· οὐχὶ δηναρίου συνεφώνησάς μοι;
20:13.targetText: But he answered one of them, ‘Friend, I am not being unfair to you. Did you not agree with me on one denarius?

groups.note: In ὁ δέ the article serves as the pronoun he.
ἀποκριθεὶς … εἶπεν, "answering, said", is condensed to answered.

20:14.sourceText: ἆρον τὸ σὸν καὶ ὕπαγε· θέλω δὲ τούτῳ τῷ ἐσχάτῳ δοῦναι ὡς καὶ σοί·
20:14.targetText: Take your pay and go. I want to give this last man the same as I gave you.

groups.note: τὸ σόν, "what is yours", is rendered your pay.
ὡς καί, "as also", is rendered the same as.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the verb that the elliptical Greek ("as also to you") leaves understood.

20:15.sourceText: οὐκ ἔξεστίν μοι ὃ θέλω ποιῆσαι ἐν τοῖς ἐμοῖς; ἢ ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου πονηρός ἐστιν ὅτι ἐγὼ ἀγαθός εἰμι;
20:15.targetText: Do I not have the right to do as I please with what is mine? Or are you envious because I am generous?’

groups.note: ἔξεστιν, "it is permitted", is rendered have the right.
The dative μοι, "for me", becomes the subject I.
τοῖς ἐμοῖς, "my own things", is rendered what is mine.
ὁ ὀφθαλμὸς … πονηρός, "the eye … evil", is an idiom for envy.
σου, "your", becomes the subject of the idiom.

20:16.sourceText: Οὕτως ἔσονται οἱ ἔσχατοι πρῶτοι καὶ οἱ πρῶτοι ἔσχατοι.
20:16.targetText: So the last will be first, and the first will be last.”

groups.note: One ἔσονται serves both clauses; English repeats will be.

20:17.sourceText: Μέλλων δὲ ἀναβαίνειν Ἰησοῦς εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα παρέλαβεν τοὺς δώδεκα κατ’ ἰδίαν, καὶ ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς
20:17.targetText: As Jesus was going up to Jerusalem, He took the twelve disciples aside and said,

groups.note: N1904 reads Μέλλων ἀναβαίνειν, "being about to go up"; BSB's wording matches the reading ἀναβαίνων, "going up".
κατ’ ἰδίαν, "privately", is one idiom.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
BSB leaves ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ ("on the way") unexpressed.
BSB leaves the addressees αὐτοῖς ("to them") unexpressed.

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB follows the reading τοὺς δώδεκα μαθητάς; N1904 has no μαθητάς.

20:18.sourceText: Ἰδοὺ ἀναβαίνομεν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα, καὶ ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου παραδοθήσεται τοῖς ἀρχιερεῦσιν καὶ γραμματεῦσιν, καὶ κατακρινοῦσιν αὐτὸν εἰς θάνατον,
20:18.targetText: “Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be delivered over to the chief priests and scribes. They will condemn Him to death

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The καί is not expressed; BSB starts a new sentence with They.

20:19.sourceText: καὶ παραδώσουσιν αὐτὸν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν εἰς τὸ ἐμπαῖξαι καὶ μαστιγῶσαι καὶ σταυρῶσαι, καὶ τῇ τρίτῃ ἡμέρᾳ ἐγερθήσεται.
20:19.targetText: and will deliver Him over to the Gentiles to be mocked and flogged and crucified. And on the third day He will be raised to life.”

groups.note: The dative τοῖς ἔθνεσιν supplies to.
εἰς τό with the infinitive expresses purpose; BSB renders the active infinitives as passives.

targetPhrases.text: He will be raised to life

20:20.sourceText: Τότε προσῆλθεν αὐτῷ ἡ μήτηρ τῶν υἱῶν Ζεβεδαίου μετὰ τῶν υἱῶν αὐτῆς προσκυνοῦσα καὶ αἰτοῦσά τι ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ.
20:20.targetText: Then the mother of Zebedee’s sons came to Jesus with her sons and knelt down to make a request of Him.

groups.note: αὐτῷ, "to him", is rendered with the name Jesus.
The genitive τῶν υἱῶν supplies of; Zebedee’s renders Ζεβεδαίου.
αἰτοῦσά τι, "asking something", is rendered to make a request.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The καί joining kneeling and asking is not expressed; BSB renders the asking as purpose.

unmappedTarget.reason: English coordinator; the participle προσκυνοῦσα is rendered as the finite verb knelt down.

20:21.sourceText: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῇ Τί θέλεις; λέγει αὐτῷ Εἰπὲ ἵνα καθίσωσιν οὗτοι οἱ δύο υἱοί μου εἷς ἐκ δεξιῶν καὶ εἷς ἐξ εὐωνύμων σου ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ σου.
20:21.targetText: “What do you want?” He inquired.  She answered, “Declare that in Your kingdom one of these two sons of mine may sit at Your right hand, and the other at Your left.”

groups.note: In ὁ δέ the article serves as the pronoun He.
English one of restructures the distributive εἷς … εἷς.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
BSB leaves the addressees αὐτῇ ("to her") and αὐτῷ ("to him") unexpressed.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: N1904 has no σου after δεξιῶν ("right"); BSB's Your here matches the reading ἐκ δεξιῶν σου.

20:22.sourceText: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν Οὐκ οἴδατε τί αἰτεῖσθε. δύνασθε πιεῖν τὸ ποτήριον ὃ ἐγὼ μέλλω πίνειν; λέγουσιν αὐτῷ Δυνάμεθα.
20:22.targetText: “You do not know what you are asking,” Jesus replied. “Can you drink the cup I am going to drink?”  “We can,” the brothers answered.

groups.note: ἀποκριθεὶς … εἶπεν, "answering, said", is condensed to replied.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The relative ὅ ("which") is left implicit in English.
BSB leaves the addressee αὐτῷ ("to him") unexpressed.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject that the Greek verb ending implies.

20:23.sourceText: λέγει αὐτοῖς Τὸ μὲν ποτήριόν μου πίεσθε, τὸ δὲ καθίσαι ἐκ δεξιῶν μου καὶ ἐξ εὐωνύμων οὐκ ἔστιν ἐμὸν τοῦτο δοῦναι, ἀλλ’ οἷς ἡτοίμασται ὑπὸ τοῦ Πατρός μου.
20:23.targetText: “You will indeed drink My cup,” Jesus said. “But to sit at My right or left is not Mine to grant. These seats belong to those for whom My Father has prepared them.”

groups.note: μέν marks the first half of the μέν … δέ contrast.
The articular infinitive τὸ … καθίσαι is the subject, to sit.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the addressees αὐτοῖς ("to them") unexpressed.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The second preposition ἐξ is covered by the shared English at.
The resumptive τοῦτο ("this") is not separately expressed.
BSB starts a new sentence instead of rendering ἀλλά ("but").
BSB makes the passive agent ("by the Father") the subject of an active verb, so ὑπό and the article have no separate English word.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the speaker that the Greek verb ending implies.
English supplies the subject and verb that the elliptical Greek leaves understood.

20:24.sourceText: καὶ ἀκούσαντες οἱ δέκα ἠγανάκτησαν περὶ τῶν δύο ἀδελφῶν.
20:24.targetText: When the ten heard about this, they were indignant with the two brothers.

groups.note: The participle ἀκούσαντες is rendered as a temporal clause.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί is not separately expressed in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the object of heard.

20:25.sourceText: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς προσκαλεσάμενος αὐτοὺς εἶπεν Οἴδατε ὅτι οἱ ἄρχοντες τῶν ἐθνῶν κατακυριεύουσιν αὐτῶν καὶ οἱ μεγάλοι κατεξουσιάζουσιν αὐτῶν.
20:25.targetText: But Jesus called them aside and said, “You know that the rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them, and their superiors exercise authority over them.

groups.note: The article is rendered as the possessive their.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English coordinator; the participle προσκαλεσάμενος is rendered as the finite verb called.

20:26.sourceText: οὐχ οὕτως ἐστὶν ἐν ὑμῖν· ἀλλ’ ὃς ἐὰν θέλῃ ἐν ὑμῖν μέγας γενέσθαι, ἔσται ὑμῶν διάκονος,
20:26.targetText: It shall not be this way among you. Instead, whoever wants to become great among you must be your servant,

groups.note: N1904 has the present ἐστίν ("it is"); BSB follows the reading ἔσται ("it shall be").

20:27.sourceText: καὶ ὃς ἂν θέλῃ ἐν ὑμῖν εἶναι πρῶτος, ἔσται ὑμῶν δοῦλος·
20:27.targetText: and whoever wants to be first among you must be your slave—

20:28.sourceText: ὥσπερ ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου οὐκ ἦλθεν διακονηθῆναι, ἀλλὰ διακονῆσαι καὶ δοῦναι τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ λύτρον ἀντὶ πολλῶν.
20:28.targetText: just as the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give His life as a ransom for many.”

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

20:29.sourceText: Καὶ ἐκπορευομένων αὐτῶν ἀπὸ Ἱερειχὼ ἠκολούθησεν αὐτῷ ὄχλος πολύς.
20:29.targetText: As they were leaving Jericho, a large crowd followed Him.

groups.note: The genitive absolute ἐκπορευομένων αὐτῶν supplies As.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί is not separately expressed in this English wording.
English leaving takes Jericho as its object, so ἀπό ("from") has no separate word.

20:30.sourceText: καὶ ἰδοὺ δύο τυφλοὶ καθήμενοι παρὰ τὴν ὁδόν, ἀκούσαντες ὅτι Ἰησοῦς παράγει, ἔκραξαν λέγοντες Κύριε, ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς, υἱὸς Δαυείδ.
20:30.targetText: And there were two blind men sitting beside the road. When they heard that Jesus was passing by, they cried out, “Lord, Son of David, have mercy on us!”

groups.note: ἰδού ("look") introduces the scene; BSB renders it with the presentational there were.

unmappedSource.reason: The participle λέγοντες ("saying") only introduces the quotation.

20:31.sourceText: ὁ δὲ ὄχλος ἐπετίμησεν αὐτοῖς ἵνα σιωπήσωσιν· οἱ δὲ μεῖζον ἔκραξαν λέγοντες Κύριε, ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς, υἱὸς Δαυείδ.
20:31.targetText: The crowd admonished them to be silent, but they cried out all the louder, “Lord, Son of David, have mercy on us!”

groups.note: ἵνα with the subjunctive is rendered as an infinitive.
In οἱ δέ the article serves as the pronoun they.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The participle λέγοντες ("saying") only introduces the quotation.

20:32.sourceText: καὶ στὰς ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐφώνησεν αὐτοὺς καὶ εἶπεν Τί θέλετε ποιήσω ὑμῖν;
20:32.targetText: Jesus stopped and called them. “What do you want Me to do for you?” He asked.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The καί before εἶπεν is not expressed; BSB places He asked after the question.

unmappedTarget.reason: English coordinator; the participle στάς is rendered as the finite verb stopped.

20:33.sourceText: λέγουσιν αὐτῷ Κύριε, ἵνα ἀνοιγῶσιν οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ ἡμῶν.
20:33.targetText: “Lord,” they answered, “let our eyes be opened.”

groups.note: ἵνα with the subjunctive voices the request, rendered let.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the addressee αὐτῷ ("to him") unexpressed.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

20:34.sourceText: σπλαγχνισθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἥψατο τῶν ὀμμάτων αὐτῶν, καὶ εὐθέως ἀνέβλεψαν καὶ ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ.
20:34.targetText: Moved with compassion, Jesus touched their eyes, and at once they received their sight and followed Him.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
